subject: Deckhook: urgent — p99/p95 latency spike after model rollout
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan@deckhook.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: jim.park@deckhook.ai
Date: 2028-06-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production latency spike after model swap

Jasmine —

We started seeing a big jump in tail latency ~30m after your team flipped the A/B flag to push v2.4 to 20% of traffic. p95 moved from ~180ms to ~420ms and p99 jumps to 1.2s+ for many prompt shapes. Our users are experiencing timeouts on interactive flows.

Attached is a quick trace screenshot and a CSV of sampled logs. Can you confirm whether v2.4 introduced any new kernel or KV-cache behavior that could explain this? We need either immediate rollback or a mitigation plan — this is impacting our demo environment and a handful of paying customers.

— Ethan (Deckhook SRE)

Attachments: deckhook-p99-traces.png (image/png), dd-sampled-logs-20280622.csv (text/csv)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan@deckhook.ai>, Maya Ross <maya.ross@deckhook.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-22T08:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deckhook: urgent — p99/p95 latency spike after model rollout

Thanks Ethan — I’m on it. I’ve looped in Marissa (on-call ops), Ben (Sales lead), and Karthik (runtime).

Quick context: we pushed v2.4 yesterday as a performance-forward candidate but with some kernel changes for longer KV lifetimes and a different batching heuristic. Canary was at 10–20% for the last 12 hours and metrics looked stable until ~07:40 PT.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Marissa to confirm canary traffic split and initiate a rollback to v2.3 if abnormal latency persists.
- Karthik to review runtime logs and any kernel fallback signals; look for GC/KV hot paths.
- I’ll ask for a short maintenance window if rollback is required — will provide ETA.

Please keep the sampled logs coming; the CSV is helpful. I’ll update within 30m.

— Jasmine

Signature: Jasmine Liu | Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-22T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deckhook: urgent — p99/p95 latency spike after model rollout

Checked the rollout dashboard: Canary traffic was increased to 20% at 2028-06-22T06:50:12Z, then steady. At 07:38 PT we see an abrupt spike in queueing and tail latency for the model family serving v2.4. No automated rollback triggers fired because error-rate thresholds were not breached.

I’m going to pause the canary now (scale to 0% for v2.4) and shift all traffic back to v2.3 across the hosted API shard that serves Deckhook (shard-us-west-2-3). Will post confirmation when complete.

— Marissa (on-call infra)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-22T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deckhook: urgent — p99/p95 latency spike after model rollout

Thanks — quick notes from the runtime side after an initial log scrub:
- v2.4 introduced a small change in the kv-cache eviction policy to keep prefixes longer (intended to reduce warm-start cost). Under some prompt distributions (many unique short prompts) this increases memory churn and increases async GC cycles on the serving nodes.
- We also shipped a kernel heuristic that attempts coalesced attention for mixed-seq batches; that path falls back to a slower generic kernel when sequences are highly heterogeneous. The fallback appears to be triggering at higher rates for Deckhook’s workload mix, causing CPU/GPU sync delays.

Immediate mitigations we can do now:
1) Force kv-cache TTL back to previous value for the Deckhook canary (fast config flip).
2) Disable coalesced-attention heuristic for the affected model variant (requires a quick feature flag flip).

I recommend rolling back the canary until we can apply (1) and (2) as a scoped mitigation. I’ll prepare the runtime patch and a postmortem action list.

— Karthik
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan@deckhook.ai>, Maya Ross <maya.ross@deckhook.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-22T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deckhook: urgent — p99/p95 latency spike after model rollout

Ethan/Maya —

We’ve paused the canary and shifted traffic back to v2.3 for your shard at 09:20 PT. You should see p95/p99 recover to previous ranges within a few seconds as connections drain.

We’re treating this as an operational escalation and looping in Grace (Head of Customer Reliability) to brief execs if Deckhook requests crediting or a formal incident report. Ben is on the thread for commercial coordination.

Next steps we’ll take today:
- Runtime will flip kv-cache TTL and disable the coalesced-attention heuristic for a scoped re-test (Karthik).
- If scoped re-test looks stable, we’ll schedule a controlled canary re-run with tighter telemetry and an automated rollback rule (Marissa).
- We’ll provide an incident write-up by EOD with root cause, mitigation, and customer impact.

Do you want us to open a joint incident bridge now or would you prefer status updates by email?

— Jasmine
From: Ethan Park <ethan@deckhook.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Ross <maya.ross@deckhook.ai>, jim.park@deckhook.ai, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-22T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deckhook: urgent — p99/p95 latency spike after model rollout

Jasmine/Team —

Thanks for the fast response and rollback. After traffic shifted back we see p95 return to ~170–200ms and p99 back under 500ms within the shard. We appreciate the rapid mitigation.

We’d like a post-incident deck and confirmation on the patch you’ll run (kv-ttl rollback + heuristic toggle). Also please confirm whether any customers beyond Deckhook might have seen short-lived tail spikes and whether Redwood will proactively notify them.

If you decide to run a re-test, we request a short maintenance window and the ability to opt-out specific customer keys.

— Ethan

[Thread status: canary paused; postmortem pending]
